newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan January M2 money supply up 9.35 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan January M2 money supply up 9.35 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's M2 money supply grew 9.35 percent in January compared to January 1996 under a newly adjusted definition of the island's broadest money supply measure, the central bank said on Monday.

The year-on-year increase put M2 growth within the central bank's 9-14 percent target zone for the first time since August 1995 and slightly above the average 9.1 percent rise forecast by a February 21 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.

Economists said the new M2 definition, which expands the category to include several additional types of money, would add one to 1.5 percentage points to M2 growth -- all but ensuring that January's M2 growth would fall into the target zone.
M2 had risen only 7.95 percent year-on-year in December.
The central bank said it revised its definition of M2 to reflect Taiwan's liberalising financial infrastructure.
According to the central bank's previous definition, M1A was cash, checking accounts and passbook deposits and M1B was M1A plus savings accounts. M2 was M1B plus quasi-money.

Under the revision, the central bank said it was retaining its M1A and M1B definitions, but redefining M2 as M1B plus time deposits, foreign currency deposits, postal funds, repurchase agreement trade outstanding and foreigners' Taiwan dollar holdings.

The new M2 definition uses post offices' total deposits instead of their redeposits in banks, adds repurchase agreement trade outstanding and foreigners' Taiwan dollar holdings, and deletes the net value of financial bonds, savings bonds and treasury bills and foreign-currency trust funds.
